idFamilies.JAVA-XNA: A gap between CNA-Java and the original XNA 4.0 contract.
idFamilies.JAVA-NATIVE: A gap at the CNA C ABI boundary: a route, a shape or a verification.
idFamilies.JAVA-EXT: A CNA capability outside XNA 4.0, belonging under org.openeggbert.cna.extensions.
idFamilies.JAVA-TEMPLATE: Work in the sibling cna-java-template consumer canary.

tasks.title: Inventory the Content Pipeline build-time profile
tasks.authority: the seven Content Pipeline assemblies, SHA-256 pinned in xna40-content-pipeline.json
tasks.currentState: Measured. 128 reference types and 743 members; 125 of the types are absent and 3 are already present from the runtime projection. By namespace: Graphics 47, the framework 32, Processors 28, Intermediate 7, Compiler 5, Audio 5, MSBuild Tasks 4.
tasks.expectedState: A decision, recorded with its evidence in docs/content-pipeline-decision.md: partial/interop. CNA-Java consumes compiled content and does not reimplement Microsoft's build-time pipeline. Four measured reasons, none of them size: two namespaces need MSBuild and System.Xml types the pinned corpus does not contain; the ten importers wrap Windows-only native technology whose bytes cannot be reproduced; every ContentTypeWriter's one abstract member returns a CLR assembly-qualified reader name, so emitting .xnb from Java would produce files no XNA runtime reads; and CNA already ships its own compiler and format, which the binding now consumes through org.openeggbert.cna.extensions.content.
tasks.note: The profile stays pinned and is deliberately not measured against the runtime target: a build-time contract is not a runtime regression gate.

tasks.expectedState: org.openeggbert.cna.extensions.graphics projects the seven identities, the render pipeline settings, the physically based material and the ASCII, CRT and depth post-process effects. Availability is truthful and NOT_SUPPORTED keeps its own identity.

tasks.title: Expose CNA's runtime and device extensions
tasks.authority: core_ext.h, devices.h, sensors.h, input_haptics.h, input_joystick.h, input_text.h, input_cursor.h, input_devices.h
tasks.currentState: Six families are projected: the runtime's own identity and logger, the host devices, typed text plus the mouse cursor, the four host motion sensors, device and sensor enumeration with hot plug, and raw joysticks, haptics and the modern game-pad, keyboard, mouse and touch capabilities.
tasks.expectedState: Typed Java facades under the extension namespace, never inside Microsoft.Xna.Framework. Availability is CNA's answer everywhere: an absent sensor reports NotSupported and refuses a reading rather than answering zeros, a closed haptic device is a safe no-op, and an unconnected joystick captures empty.

tasks.title: Expose the .cnb content format
tasks.currentState: Done. 248 of the 272 routes are bound and reached, and the loader registry -- the one part that needed a decision rather than more binding -- is answered in docs/cnb-loader-registry-decision.md. Eight asset families read and write, five of them crossing to the XNA type a game uses. The model family is complete. CnbImport reads PNG, JPEG, WAV and DDS; Cnj compiles the .cnj documents that say what to do with them, reporting absorbed sources and external references for a build system. CnbLoaders dispatches a document to the loader that may read it, implementing CNA's identity rule rather than projecting its C-callback table.
tasks.expectedState: Achieved. What stays unbound is stated with its reason rather than left open: the loader registration and invoke routes need a C callback and return a void* no Java call could receive; cna_cnb_model_add_animation takes a nested descriptor graph the generator refuses rather than guesses at, so animations are read rather than written; and cna_cnb_texture_data_select_representation takes a predicate callback.
tasks.note: Every .cnb fixture is produced by CNA's own encoder and read back by CNA's own parser, so a successful read means the file is real. The importer and .cnj fixtures are deliberately the opposite -- a PNG written by the JDK, a WAV and a DDS and a BMP written from their published layouts, JSON written by the test -- because there the source format is what is under test and a CNA-authored input would prove nothing. The model family was probed in C first: tools/native-abi/probes/cnb_model_roundtrip.c.

tasks.title: Use the whole-buffer vertex upload route
tasks.currentState: The route is loaded, so the library must export it, but no JNI entry point reaches it: SetData always takes the windowed form.
tasks.expectedState: An upload that starts at the beginning takes CNA's whole-buffer route; a windowed one takes the windowed route. Both are now reached, and boundButUnreached is empty.

tasks.title: Bind the native Model routes behind the managed XNB model graph
tasks.currentState: 127 routes deferred; Load<Model> was managed-only, and the audit asked what native backing would add.
tasks.expectedState: The XNA Model graph reaches CNA. CnaModel.From(Model) builds CNA's own model over the buffers and effects the XNA model already owns -- retained, not copied, so nothing is uploaded twice -- and CNA then draws it in one call and computes its bone transforms. models.h is fully classified: 184 extension candidates, 31 not useful in Java, and one deferred route, the loader JAVA-UPSTREAM-004 blocks.
tasks.note: Load<Model> deliberately stays on the managed XNB reader. XNB records the effect's type and the reader builds the BasicEffect an XNA game casts to; CNA publishes a loaded effect as a handle whose type is only a name, so routing the strict load through CNA would break (BasicEffect) part.getEffect(). The measurement is in CnaModelTests, which reads one authored .xnb through both runtimes and compares their graphs bone for bone.

tasks.title: Bind the remaining input routes
tasks.currentState: 132 routes were deferred. The audit found that none of them was an XNA-shaped route lacking backing: the whole XNA input surface -- game-pad state, capabilities and vibration, keyboard state, mouse state and position, touch state, capabilities, panel and gestures -- was already bound.
tasks.expectedState: Every input route classified with a stated reason and no deferred remainder. 39 became bound CNA extensions (modern game-pad identity, battery, light bar, trigger motors, touchpad, button labels and sensors; keyboard scancode and layout naming; mouse capture, relative mode, desktop position and the click event; mouse-driven touch emulation). The remaining 92 are NOT_USEFUL_IN_JAVA: construction, equality, hashing, string form and indexing of XNA's input value types, which are managed structs in XNA and managed values here, plus two CNA test seams.

tasks.title: Nine of cnanext's own C API smoke tests fail in the HEADLESS/NULL-audio configuration
tasks.currentState: Remeasured on 2026-08-31 against ABI 0.21.0: 99 of 104 pass, and the five that fail are CApi_CoreExtSmoke, CApi_ContentSmoke, CApi_DevicesSmoke, CApi_AudioSmoke and CApi_AudioUnavailableSmoke. Four of the original nine now pass -- CApiCoverageMatrix, CApiLimitations, CApiReleaseGate and CApi_MediaPlayerSmoke. The first run after rebuilding libcna_c_api reported nine failures again, but four of those were stale test executables compiled against 0.20 headers and linked against the 0.21 library; rebuilding the test targets was needed before the number meant anything, and that is recorded here because the same trap will catch the next reader.
tasks.expectedState: Either the suite passes in HEADLESS/HEADLESS/NULL, or cnanext records which of its tests need a different platform, renderer or audio backend. CNA-Java does not depend on it: its own 220 tests qualify what this binding uses, and CApi_ContentSmoke's failure is in the same content path JAVA-UPSTREAM-004 reproduces.

tasks.title: Project CNA's text composition and candidate events
tasks.currentState: Typed characters were projected; composition text and candidate lists were not, because each carries a string the fixed five-long event record cannot hold.
tasks.expectedState: A second transport that owns heap copies made inside CNA's callback, hands them to Java as byte arrays in one call that frees the record before it returns, and is merged with the numeric queue by a sequence stamped when CNA raised the event, so one order comes out of two queues. TextComposition and TextCandidates sit on top of it in the input extension package.
tasks.blocker: None upstream. It needs a second event transport, not a CNA change.

tasks.title: Reach or unbind the 162 routes no Java call site touches
tasks.currentState: 162 bound routes had a generated JNI entry point that no Java source called. All of them are resolved: seven were reached and 155 unbound with a rule saying why. boundWithoutJavaCallSite is 0 and nativeCoverageCheck now fails on it, so it cannot regrow. Bound routes went 1,570 to 1,418 and XNA_BACKING 976 to 985.
tasks.expectedState: Every bound route reaches a Java call site, or is unbound with a stated reason. The reasons are families rather than one-offs: PacketReader and PacketWriter stay managed BinaryReader and BinaryWriter so Position and Length keep XNA's meaning over one cursor; a Begin/End pair is projected over CNA's synchronous route because its asynchronous form completes before its own begin returns; value construction and equality are Java's as they are for the vector families; a read-only collection's mutators can have no call site because the Java member throws as XNA's does; a factory for an object the projection receives has nothing to make; and CNA's application-rendered Guide, its avatar rendering and a discovered session's address are extensions XNA has no member for.
tasks.blocker: None. It is measurement plus per-family judgement, not an upstream change.
tasks.note: Three reaches were real gaps rather than tidying: a failed join now raises XNA's NetworkSessionJoinException carrying the error CNA recorded instead of a generic failure with a Java default, and a whole-array send or receive takes CNA's whole-buffer route as VertexBuffer.SetData already did. A fourth was refused by the full-profile gate: asking CNA for a gamer collection's membership would have declared contains and indexOf on GamerCollection, which CLR's does not declare.

tasks.title: cna_content_manager_load_model produces a model that segfaults during teardown
tasks.currentState: Loading any .xnb whose meshes have parts through CNA's own content manager gives a model that crashes when it is released. Reproduced in C with no Java involved: cna_game_create, cna_game_get_graphics_device, cna_content_manager_create, cna_content_manager_load_model("cube") over cnanext's own tests/assets/xnb/monogame/windows/uncompressed/BlenderDefaultCube.xnb, then cna_model_destroy. SIGSEGV in Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics::ModelMeshPart::setTagProperty called from (anonymous namespace)::PartResource::~PartResource. The crash does not need the model to be walked first, and it also happens when the caller never destroys the model and lets the content manager and game tear it down, so there is no calling order that avoids it. A model assembled by hand with cna_model_create_with_parents over a mesh with a part destroys cleanly, so the fault is on the content-load path rather than in the model family.
tasks.expectedState: A content-loaded model releases without faulting, so a binding can offer CNA's own loader.
tasks.blocker: cnanext content: PartResource's destructor reaches a ModelMeshPart whose owner is already gone. cnanext's own CApi_ContentSmoke fixtures are models with one bone and no meshes, which is why the path is uncovered upstream.

tasks.title: Three value types leaked the CNA handles they owned
tasks.currentState: Fixed, and it was three types rather than one. NetworkSessionProperties' public constructor, all four AvatarDescription paths, and every LeaderboardEntry created an owned CNA handle that nothing released; none of the three is IDisposable in XNA, so a game had nothing to close and no way to know. LeaderboardReader.getEntries was the worst: every entry CNA hands out is an owned copy, so the leak grew with each call of an ordinary getter. Measured: cna_network_session_properties_destroy answers CNA_RESULT_THREAD from any thread but the creating one, so a Cleaner could not release any of them either.
tasks.expectedState: org.openeggbert.cna.internal.NativeDeferredRelease records the handle when the Java object becomes unreachable and the owning thread releases it at the next FrameworkDispatcher.Update, which is where this binding already does deferred native work. A session-owned list registers nothing, because the session frees it.

tasks.title: Two gates could not see an ABI migration go wrong
tasks.currentState: Done. The generator keeps an unwind list of unconditional releases in acquisition order, and every early return replays it in reverse. It could not reuse the existing cleanup list, which is why this was recorded rather than fixed in passing: some of those statements are guarded on the call's result, which is not declared yet at the point an acquisition can fail.
tasks.expectedState: Every early return releases what it holds, and the success path still releases each acquisition exactly once. Three tool tests check both, on the four-array route that made the defect ordinary rather than rare.

tasks.title: Project the gamer-services capabilities XNA has no member for
tasks.currentState: Done, within the boundary stated below. The Guide slice projects the pending on-screen keyboard and message box, CNA's renderer for them, the outcomes a game reports back and the achievements pane (16 routes). The net slice answers where a session is and adds the direction XNA cannot reach at all -- describing a session at a known address so NetworkSession.Join can take it. The avatar slice projects the appearance colours a real-rendered avatar is drawn in, the clip an animation plays, and the clip and content names behind XNA's canonical presets and body types (9 routes).
tasks.expectedState: Three coherent slices under org.openeggbert.cna.extensions. CNA's Guide hands the application the pending on-screen keyboard or message box and asks it to draw, where XNA's Guide draws itself: 14 routes, and the useful shape is a typed pending-request record plus a render call, not a projection of the raw routes. CNA's avatar layer exposes real rendering and the clip and content names behind the canonical presets: 10 routes. And a discovered session carries the host and port it was found at, which AvailableNetworkSession does not name: 4 routes.
tasks.blocker: None. It needs an API design per slice, not a CNA change.
tasks.note: Two avatar routes are deliberately still unbound: cna_avatar_renderer_enable_real_rendering_ext and cna_avatar_renderer_draw_real_ext want a CNA_SkinnedModelEXT, which this projection has no Java type for. Exposing them with a raw long handle would be an API a game cannot safely use, and half of a two-step contract is worse than none. JAVA-EXT-007 finishes them.

tasks.title: Project CNA's skinned model, and finish real avatar rendering on top of it
tasks.currentState: Measured against the live headers: the generator plans 23 of the 26 cna_skinned_model_ext_* routes and refuses three. cna_skinned_model_ext_create and cna_skinned_model_ext_set_clip take descriptors whose fields are pointers to arrays of descriptors -- clip to tracks to keyframes -- and cna_skinned_model_ext_create additionally carries three arrays governed by one count. The arrayLengths declaration added for the second shape covers set_skeleton; the nested descriptor graph is the one that is not covered.
tasks.expectedState: A SkinnedModel extension type with the skeleton, the clips and the computed bone transforms a game needs. XNA 4.0 has no skeletal animation at all -- Microsoft shipped it as a separate sample -- so this is a capability the reference API never had.
tasks.blocker: set_clip is the only door a clip can go through, and no route takes a clip handle instead. Without it a Java skinned model can have a skeleton and parts but no clips, and compute_bone_transforms has nothing to compute, so the 23 plannable routes do not add up to a usable feature. Either the generator learns nested descriptor graphs -- a marshaller for a variable-depth pointer graph, which is a much larger and less provable step than the two shapes added so far -- or CNA grows a handle-based way to put a clip into a skinned model.
tasks.note: cnanext's own AvatarsSmoke can only check that real rendering refuses an invalid model, because the C container has no skinned model to hand it either.

tasks.title: Project CNA's engine layer, one family at a time
tasks.currentState: 246 of the 857 routes are bound and reached: the layer's revision, the LOD group, the debug renderer's geometry and all six of its gizmos, the full render-pipeline settings value, the frustum culler, the instanced renderer, the GPU timer, the three light value types, the whole of clustered forward lighting, all four shadow maps, and light probes with their volumes. Families are chosen by measurement -- tools/native-abi/probes/engine_layer_families.c, which runs two passes and creates a real game to borrow a device from. Qualification: LOD group, frustum culler, lights, shadow fitting and light probes VERIFIED_PURE; settings pure arithmetic; debug renderer, instanced renderer, clustered lighting and shadow-map state VERIFIED_HEADLESS_GAME; GPU timer, the clustered compute path and shadow casting NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_RENDERER with their refusals qualified rather than skipped.
tasks.expectedState: More families as each earns a consumer and can be qualified. The layer is a modern renderer -- clustered forward lighting, cascaded and contact and cube shadows, SSAO, SSR, tonemapping, auto-exposure, atmospheric sky, decals, particles, debug draw, instancing, light probes -- none of which XNA 4.0 has any counterpart for, so every family is an addition rather than a member being filled in. It is 857 routes and the wrong way to spend them is mechanically: a coherent Java type per family, with the parts that cannot be honestly qualified here left unbound and said so.
tasks.blocker: None, but most families need a real graphics device. The probe found that debug draw and the particle system both refuse an invalid one, so those tests have to run inside a Game, and anything whose result is a rendered image cannot be checked in a HEADLESS renderer at all -- which has to be stated rather than asserted around.
tasks.note: LodGroup deliberately holds thresholds rather than mesh parts: the Java projection's ModelMeshPart is a managed object with no native handle, so there is nothing to hand CNA and nothing meaningful to receive. selectIndex returns the level and the game draws what it keeps at that index. Five of DebugDraw's six gizmo routes are bound: the three light gizmos with the lighting slice, and the cluster-slice and cascade gizmos with the families whose handles they take. All six are bound now. cna_shadow_cascade_state_ext_init is deliberately unbound: no route in the whole C API consumes a CNA_ShadowCascadeStateEXT, so binding it would produce a value nothing can be handed to. Nothing in DebugDrawTests claims a line was drawn -- this qualification has a HEADLESS renderer -- only that the queue holds what was put in it, which is the part a game's own logic depends on. FrustumCuller is VERIFIED_PURE: it needs no device, and its evidence is agreement with XNA's own BoundingFrustum across a 125-box grid. Which XNA test matters -- CNA's culler is Contains(box) != Disjoint, the six-plane test, and XNA's Intersects is GJK. They disagree on boxes near a frustum corner, always with the plane test being the one that drops, and the projection measures that divergence rather than hiding it. The first version of the test used a camera at the origin looking down -Z, whose view matrix is the identity -- against which a planted view/projection swap passed. The camera is off-axis now. The two caster-effect accessors on each shadow map are deliberately unbound: applyCaster is the operation a game needs, and a borrowed engine effect has no Java facade with a coherent lifetime yet. The light-probe baker's thirteen routes are unbound: its three bake routes each take a scene-draw callback the generator refuses, and a baker that cannot bake reports only its own configuration.

tasks.title: Decide what RenderPipelineSettings projects, now that there are two of them
tasks.currentState: Decided and done. CNA's own header settles it: the frozen ten-field CNA_RenderPipelineSettings cannot grow inside an ABI major, so the complete shape arrived under a new name, and every engine-layer route that takes settings -- including the pipeline's own get and set -- takes the larger one. RenderPipelineSettingsExt projects it, with all fifty fields and CNA's own prose on each. RenderPipelineSettings keeps its name and its narrower job, because it is a faithful projection of a CNA type that still exists.
tasks.expectedState: Achieved. normalize() is the method that earns the type: CNA warns that writing a field is not the same as the engine storing it -- thirty-one of them correct their input -- and normalize asks what would actually be stored. applyFrom() applies serialized text and reports how many fields it recognised, which is what a console command or a config file wants.
tasks.blocker: None technically -- all three value routes plan cleanly. It needs the design call first, because growing a published type from 10 properties to 50 is not something to do by accident, and it decides whether the existing one keeps its name.
tasks.note: Found while looking for an engine-layer family that could be qualified with no renderer. The three settings value routes are exactly that -- pure functions on a structure -- and they were bound, then unbound again when the two structures turned out to be different. Binding them against the smaller Java type would have silently truncated forty fields.

tasks.title: Four clustered engine-layer routes document a game handle and take a graphics device
tasks.currentState: cna_clustered_light_set_create, cna_clustered_light_grid_create, cna_clustered_light_assignment_create and cna_clustered_shadow_policy_create each name their first parameter `game` and document it as "the owning game". Measured in C by tools/native-abi/probes/engine_layer_families.c: all four answer CNA_RESULT_INVALID_HANDLE for an owned game handle and for a callback-borrowed one, and all four succeed when given the game's graphics device. The implementation resolves the parameter with GetBorrowedGraphicsDevice, so the header's parameter name and its prose are both wrong.
tasks.expectedState: Either the header says graphics device, or the routes accept a game. Until then CNA-Java passes the graphics device and its own documentation says why, because a projection that repeated the header's word would hand callers a handle CNA refuses.
tasks.blocker: Upstream documentation defect in cnanext; CNA-Java cannot fix it and does not need it fixed to proceed.
tasks.note: Not a functional blocker for the lighting slice: the behaviour is usable and now measured. It is recorded so the next reader does not spend the same hour, and so that a future CNA that changes the parameter to match its documentation is noticed rather than silently breaking every clustered call.

tasks.title: A documented INVALID_STATE refusal arrives as INTERNAL, because the exception barrier has no logic_error arm
tasks.currentState: cna_instanced_renderer_ext_draw documents CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE for a renderer that cannot instance with the per-instance fallback off, and CnaCApiEngineLayer.cpp's own comment says the exception barrier maps the std::logic_error the engine throws to that result. CallWithExceptionBarrier has no std::logic_error arm; the throw reaches catch (const std::exception&) and returns CNA_RESULT_INTERNAL (12). Reproduced in pure C by tools/native-abi/probes/instanced_draw_refusal.c, which prints INTERNAL (12) against a documented INVALID_STATE (3).
tasks.expectedState: Either the barrier grows a std::logic_error arm mapping to INVALID_STATE, or the engine throws something the barrier already maps. Until then a game cannot tell a refusal it can act on -- turn the fallback on -- from a defect inside CNA, which is exactly the distinction CNA_RESULT_INTERNAL exists to make.
tasks.blocker: Upstream defect in cnanext's C API exception barrier; CNA-Java cannot fix it.
tasks.note: CNA-Java works around it soundly rather than by matching on the message: InstancedRenderer.draw asks the renderer its own two questions on the failure path only -- can it instance, is the fallback on -- and raises IllegalStateException when they explain the refusal, keeping CNA's failure and its real result code as the cause. The workaround costs nothing on the success path and stops working correctly the moment CNA fixes the result, at which point it simply becomes redundant rather than wrong. Likely wider than this one route: std::logic_error is thrown in more than one place in the engine layer.

tasks.title: A cube shadow map's face passes do not open on a renderer that cannot cast, though CNA says they do
tasks.authority: CNA's own startup log against measured behaviour
tasks.currentState: CNA logs "CNA::Graphics::CubeShadowMap: point shadows are unavailable on this renderer. Face passes still open and close, and the cube keeps meaning nothing occludes, so the frame renders unshadowed rather than failing." On the HEADLESS renderer they do not: cna_cube_shadow_map_begin returns CNA_RESULT_INTERNAL (12) with the diagnostic "HeadlessRenderer::SetViewport: rectangle (0,0,512x512) exceeds the current target's bounds (800x480)", and the matching end fails too. cna_shadow_map_begin and _end on the same renderer, at the same quality and therefore the same size, both succeed -- so the difference is binding a cube face rather than a 2D target. Measured in C by tools/native-abi/probes/engine_layer_families.c.
tasks.expectedState: Either the headless renderer binds a cube face the way it binds a 2D target, or the log stops promising that face passes open. As it stands a game that follows CNA's own advice -- run the shadow pass unconditionally and let it do nothing -- crashes on point shadows and not on directional ones.
tasks.blocker: Upstream defect in cnanext's headless renderer; CNA-Java cannot fix it.
tasks.note: CubeShadowMap's documentation states the difference rather than hiding it, and ShadowTests asserts the current refusal when isSupported() is false -- so an upstream fix shows up as a failing test rather than going unnoticed. The result is CNA_RESULT_INTERNAL again, the same missing std::logic_error arm JAVA-UPSTREAM-006 records.
